answer: An agent marketplace allocates jobs by each agent’s share of tokens locked in escrow, rather than giving every identity an equal turn. If an attacker splits 100 tokens among agents named jade, zephyr, and glacier, their combined selection probability stays the same as one agent holding 100 tokens. To capture more jobs, the attacker must acquire and lock more tokens for 30 days, tying up capital instead of gaining influence by creating accounts.
